definitions.meaning: an informal British word for a fish-and-chip shop
British slang for a joiner or woodworker

explanation.surface: A takeaway shop needs someone to fit its counters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are British slang: a chip shop selling fried fish, and a tradesman who works with wood.

clue.text: Carla may cook this sea food

indicators.note: to cook something is to work it up, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion that Carla might prepare a seafood dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' rearranges the letters of CARLA MAY; 'this' links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid prepared as food, a variant spelling of the Italian-derived dish name.

clue.text: Directed to centre where patients are housed

parts.note: something housed is kept in, so the word gives in
hospital patients lie on wards

explanation.surface: Directions in a hospital pointing to the middle of the building where the sick are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards the inside or middle is the adverb sense of this direction word.

parts.note: to part is to separate
a hen is a layer of eggs
on can mean over, as in placed on top of

explanation.surface: An instruction to peel a layer away from an ancient Greek building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum, but it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The great temple to Athena stands on the Acropolis in Athens, so it is the classic Athenian temple.

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
grace means favour or goodwill

explanation.surface: A duchess succeeds in gaining some lady's approval.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal style of address used when speaking of a duchess in Britain.

definitions.meaning: lessons for grown-ups held after work hours
read cryptically as making social ranks level or equal

explanation.surface: A claim that night school courses help bring about a fairer society.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-school lessons for grown-ups, and literally levelling out social strata.

definitions.meaning: to arrange or organise something, as an event is got up

explanation.surface: An instruction to get ready to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to organise or arrange something and to rise to one's feet.

clue.text: A local politician familiar with being indicted

parts.note: CC is a county councillor
used to something means familiar with it

explanation.surface: A council member who is used to facing charges.
explanation.walkthrough: CC stands for county councillor, a member of a British local authority; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person formally charged with a crime has been accused, a close synonym.

clue.text: She has little time in Surrey town

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is placed inside the town name

parts.note: Esher is a town in Surrey, a county south-west of London
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman spends a short while in a suburban commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: ESHER is a commuter town in Surrey, a county south-west of London; 'little time' gives T, which sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and any female name can be clued by the pronoun for a woman.

parts.note: called means named
taken as written
good shots are marksmen

explanation.surface: Someone listed the snipers as they had been ordered to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in charge and give the orders.

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and a beast that lows is a lower
a case is a container

explanation.surface: A tidy box for storing short notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle; a cow lows, so it is a LOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers kept the minuscule type in the bottom tray, so the term names non-capital letters.

clue.text: Understood attic was to be converted

indicators.note: a loft conversion remodels the space, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: It was implicitly agreed that the loft would be turned into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit agreement is implied or understood without being stated.

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: martial means warlike or bellicose

explanation.surface: An official who turns totally aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like totally, but it signals a word said aloud: MARTIAL, warlike, is heard the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Officials who organise events, such as at a race meeting, are called stewards or marshals.

clue.text: I am over the hill, full stop!

parts.note: contracted to I'm
passé means past one's best, over the hill

explanation.surface: An ageing person's exasperated outburst at being past it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation where progress comes to a complete halt.

clue.text: Trespass again to procure plant extract

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again
to trespass is to sin, as in the Lord's Prayer

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into land a second time to obtain a botanical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky substance exuded by trees and other plants.

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them persistently
the body of something is its main part

explanation.surface: A lowly worker consistently goes along with what most people think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it goes with 'follows' to mean DOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge doing the menial tasks is a British colloquial term for a servant of all work.

parts.note: a bill is a charge to pay
the board manages a company

explanation.surface: Company directors charging for advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor hoarding for posters is space bought to advertise.

clue.text: Intend to go into action if humiliated

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a deed is an action
to mean is to intend

explanation.surface: A person plans to take action if put down.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, so demeaned means humiliated.

indicators.note: the writer's name is made from these letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: A French author originating in the Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges SHETLAND, the islands north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name of Marie-Henri Beyle, French novelist of The Red and the Black.

clue.text: He carries round a small kitchen item

indicators.note: one piece goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: a toter is one who carries

explanation.surface: A man brings around a little appliance for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts TOTER around A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric appliance for browning bread, found in a kitchen.

definitions.meaning: to abandon or go away from

explanation.surface: A vacation spent in the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abandon someone and authorised time off.

indicators.note: to dog is to follow, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: big as in large-bosomed
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: Problems pursue a well-endowed housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dogs' looks like the subject's action on the maid, but it means follows: the trouble word trails behind. Abigail became a byword for a lady's maid from a character in Beaumont and Fletcher's The Scornful Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a lady's maid, from a character in a seventeenth-century play.

clue.text: RAF officer longing for a side of bacon

parts.note: FL is short for Flight Lieutenant
an itch is a longing

explanation.surface: An air force officer craving a slab of bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a cured side of pork.

parts.note: slip-on shoes whose name also describes lazy people, so they suit lazy people

explanation.surface: Recommending comfortable shoes for lazy people.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slip-on casual shoes and people who idle about.

parts.note: facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: Equipment left behind for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's stand holding the canvas is equipment meant for the artist.

clue.text: Coach returns and players calm down

indicators.note: the word turns back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a coach is a bus
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: A coach comes back and the team relaxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings or storms that subside settle and calm down.

clue.text: In short, it used to curtail a Roman emperor

indicators.note: the emperor's name lies inside the run of words
the words are cut down at the ends to leave only the run inside

explanation.surface: A remark on how a Roman ruler was briefly cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'short, it used', trimmed at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flavian emperor who ruled Rome from 79 to 81 AD.

parts.note: over means finished
having a gain, read as a gain

explanation.surface: Ending up in the black yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repeated another time.

clue.text: Husband with no weapons is no threat

parts.note: without arms

explanation.surface: An unarmed married man poses no danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something posing no threat is innocuous or safe.

clue.text: Tot went ahead in state of confusion

parts.note: to tot up is to add
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A toddler who was in front gets muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, but it is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddled mind is said to be confused or befuddled.
